newsitem.title: MONGOLIA: Mongolia ends state controls on oil prices.
newsitem.headline: Mongolia ends state controls on oil prices.

text.p: Mongolia has ended all formal state controls on oil prices, allowing the country's main importer to raise the cost of gasoline at stations across the huge pastoral nation, officials said on Monday.
"Prices have been fully freed since September 1," a spokesman for Mongolia's near-monopoly oil supplier Neft Import Concern (NIC) told Reuters.
Oil prices in the sparsely populated nation were previously fixed by the state, but NIC was now free to set its own prices, the spokesman said.

The move followed a speech on Friday by new Prime Minister M. Enkhsaikhan in which he announced new efforts to liberalise oil prices to revive the faltering energy sector before the onset of the bitter winter.

Partly state-owned NIC, which enjoys a virtual monopoly over oil imports and distribution, had carved Mongolia's vast territory into four zones, with oil prices based on transportation distances, the spokesman said.
In the zone around the capital Ulan Bator, the price of 93 octane gasoline rose to 205 tugriks ($0.38) per litre, 76 octane petrol to 170 tugriks and diesel to 200 tugriks, he said.
In other areas of the country, prices were raised as high as 230 tugriks per litre for 93 octane, 200 tugriks for 76 octane and 230 tugriks for diesel, he said.
Nationwide average prices before the liberalisation were 164 tugriks for 93 octane, 126 tugriks for 76 octane and 151 for diesel, he added.
Aircraft fuel prices in the capital rose to 160 tugriks per litre, up from the former nationwide level of 150 tugriks, and had been set at 185 tugriks in other areas, he said.
Mongolia imports 100 percent of its oil.
